newsitem.title: GERMANY: Supermodel Schiffer angry over topless photos.
newsitem.headline: Supermodel Schiffer angry over topless photos.

text.p: German supermodel Claudia Schiffer was quoted on Monday as saying an acquaintance is trying to sell 10-year-old photographs of her sunbathing topless and she may take legal action against any publication that uses the photos.

Schiffer, who has sued magazines in the past for using unauthorised topless pictures of her, told the newspaper Bild that a man she knew briefly had taken the pictures of her when she was 17. She was sunbathing topless on a beach in Majorca.

"I was at that time not yet a public figure and took a few private snapshots," Bild quoted Schiffer as saying. "That is my private sphere and I will not let anyone break into that. I am very, very sensitive about this."
Bild said the unidentified man was now trying to sell the pictures of her clad only in bikini bottoms. It said that Schiffer was still a school girl at the time and a minor.

Bild printed two large colour pictures of the topless 17-year-old Schiffer prominently on its front page on Monday, but her hands cover her breasts in one shot and her right arm blocks most of her breasts in another picture.
"Claudia gave Bild permission to show these two pictures," the paper said. "These are harmless. But there are others and they are causing trouble."

Schiffer once launched a $17 million lawsuit against the publisher of R.O.M.E., a now-defunct New York fashion magazine for printing four pictures of her changing clothes backstage during a fashion show in Italy.

In October, Schiffer's New York-based publicist said the model was talking to her lawyers about an unauthorised advertising campaign by the Colombian army featuring a photo of her wedged between two soldiers.
Schiffer did not know the picture was going to be used for a campaign and thought it was only going to be a personal souvenir for the soldiers.
Bild said Schiffer was opposed to publication of such photos because they could harm her modelling career.
"I want to determine myself what I show in pictures," she told Bild. "I know for myself how far I can go."
